subsystems.name: Space observatory
subsystems.role: collects the starlight that has filtered through the planet's atmosphere, in wavelength channels fine enough to reveal molecules.
parts: near-infrared spectrographs such as NIRSpec and NIRISS

subsystems.name: Transit detection and ephemeris
subsystems.role: finds candidate planets and predicts exactly when each one crosses its star.

subsystems.name: Stellar characterisation
subsystems.role: establishes what the host star itself is doing, because a star's own spectrum can imitate or bury a planetary signal.

subsystems.name: Reduction pipeline
subsystems.role: turns raw detector counts into a calibrated transmission spectrum.

subsystems.name: Atmospheric retrieval
subsystems.role: works out which mix of gases, clouds and temperatures could have produced the measured spectrum.
parts: Bayesian sampler such as nested sampling

subsystems.name: Classification framework
subsystems.role: decides whether a world is plausibly Hycean, a mini-Neptune with no ocean, or something else entirely.

buildSteps.title: Find transiting candidates
buildSteps.detail: Wide-field photometric surveys watch hundreds of thousands of stars for the small periodic dimming caused by a planet crossing in front.

buildSteps.title: Measure the planet's mass
buildSteps.detail: Radial-velocity spectrographs track the star's tiny wobble; without a mass, a radius alone cannot tell a water world from a gas dwarf.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the host star
buildSteps.detail: Temperature, radius and activity are measured, and the star is monitored outside transit so its own variability can later be separated from the planet's atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Rank targets for telescope time
buildSteps.detail: Temperate sub-Neptunes orbiting small, quiet stars are prioritised, because a small star makes the atmospheric signal comparatively large and a quiet star keeps the noise down.

buildSteps.title: Observe the transits
buildSteps.detail: Telescope time is scheduled so that several transits are recorded; spectra are stacked to build the signal-to-noise ratio that a single transit cannot reach.

buildSteps.title: Reduce to a transmission spectrum
buildSteps.detail: Instrument systematics are modelled and removed, and the extra absorption caused by the planet's atmosphere is extracted wavelength bin by wavelength bin.

buildSteps.title: Retrieve the atmosphere
buildSteps.detail: Models are fitted to the spectrum to estimate molecular abundances and the temperature profile, with the sampler mapping how tightly each value is constrained.

buildSteps.title: Stress-test the result
buildSteps.detail: Synthetic signals are injected into the real data to see what the pipeline would have recovered, and competing explanations such as unocculted starspots or high-altitude haze are fitted as alternatives.

buildSteps.title: Classify and follow up
buildSteps.detail: The planet is placed in a category, then revisited at other wavelengths, across its orbit, or with ground-based high-resolution spectroscopy to see whether the classification holds.

prerequisites.why: the atmospheric signal is a few parts in ten thousand of the stellar flux and requires a cold, steady instrument above the atmosphere.
the telescope must be pointing during a window of a few hours, years in advance.
small, cool planets give faint wobbles, so many candidates still have only a radius and no density.
retrieval can only identify a molecule if its absorption is known across the observed wavelengths.
spots and faculae on the host star can imitate water or methane and are a leading cause of contested detections.

prerequisites.tech: Instrument stability at the ten-parts-per-million level
prerequisites.why: residual systematic noise, not photon statistics, currently sets the limit on what counts as a detection.

pathway.milestone: JWST transmission spectra of a handful of temperate sub-Neptunes, with tentative carbon-bearing and sulphur-bearing detections
pathway.unlocks: the first real test of whether hydrogen-rich envelopes over liquid water can be observed at all.

pathway.milestone: a uniform survey of a few tens of the best candidates analysed with one shared pipeline and shared stellar-contamination models
pathway.unlocks: classification that survives independent reanalysis rather than resting on single contested spectra.

pathway.milestone: ESA's Ariel mission, planned to survey around a thousand planets from the late 2020s
pathway.unlocks: statistics instead of anecdotes — how common each atmospheric type actually is.

pathway.milestone: extremely large ground telescopes for high-resolution spectroscopy, and later direct imaging of temperate planets
pathway.unlocks: the ability to check a candidate atmosphere without relying on a transit geometry, and eventually to look at non-transiting worlds.
